instruction: Browse the list of men's Nike socks under $20.

metadata.explanation: Task variation: Browse men's Nike socks under $20. Same pattern as original task (filter-based shopping on NBA.com), different filter criteria. Evaluator checks filter elements and URL contain the expected filters.
metadata.verification: Reuses existing check_direct_json_object metric and active_tab_html_parse getter with class&url category.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks for all 4 required filter criteria (under $20, men, socks, nike) in both HTML filter elements and URL parameters, providing comprehensive coverage
The category='class&url' approach validates both UI state (filter elements present) and URL state (filters applied), which semantically verifies the browsing task
The 'is_other_exist' check ensures no unexpected filters are applied, preventing false positives
Expected values use lowercase consistently, matching the getter's lowercase normalization logic (lines 1882-1893 in chrome.py)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding verification that actual product results are displayed (e.g., checking for product cards or result count), not just that filters are selected. Currently passes if filters are selected but no results load.

The CSS selector 'filter-selector-link' is website-specific and fragile - if NBA.com changes their class names, the evaluator will break. Consider documenting this dependency or using more robust selectors.

Add a fallback or flexibility for filter text variations (e.g., 'Under $20' vs 'under $20', 'Nike' vs 'nike') - though current lowercase normalization handles this, it's not explicit in the expected values.
